dogecoin.text: @foralldogekind @elonmusk @BillyM2k @dogecoin Doge having such a high coin count is literally the reason why it's a better currency than most cryptos. If you take away it's inflation, you're knee-capping its adoption and use as a currency. The fact that crypto people don't understand this is quite baffling

@foralldogekind @elonmusk @BillyM2k @dogecoin Of course! I believe it's important to detoxify the discourse around crypto, and the best way to do that is to have polite and reasonable discussions with others 😊

@foralldogekind @elonmusk @BillyM2k @dogecoin This article is also a good explanation as to why inflation is good for Doge

https://t.co/JW6poroY8J

@foralldogekind @elonmusk @BillyM2k @dogecoin So to put simply, if you want Doge to become the currency of Earth, putting a cap on supply is quite literally the last thing you want to do lol

If you have any thoughts or questions just let me know! I'm always happy to talk about this sorta stuff

@foralldogekind @elonmusk @BillyM2k @dogecoin If we were to cap Doge, we lose the opportunity to make it into a global currency that @elonmusk says he wants it to be. The wealthy would use it to hoard their wealth, and the average person would either have to use another crypto as a means of currency, or stick to USD

@foralldogekind @elonmusk @BillyM2k @dogecoin The ideal inflation rate, which is the inflation rate the Fed tries to achieve, is 2%

The current inflation rate Doge has right now is 3-4%, however, as time passes it will eventually reach 2%, which is literally right on the mark lol

@foralldogekind @elonmusk @BillyM2k @dogecoin I believe the same would happen w/ Doge. If the devs decided to cap Doge, people will begin to hoard it rather than use it to buy goods. We're already seeing this issue w/ bitcoin, and it hasn't even reached its cap yet!

@foralldogekind @elonmusk @BillyM2k @dogecoin If people just held their dollars indefinitely, that's less money circulating in the economy, the wealthy would hoard their wealth waaaay more than they do now, and the dollar would cease to function as a currency

@foralldogekind @elonmusk @BillyM2k @dogecoin What do you do when you own something that's guaranteed to become more valuable in the future? You hold as much as you can. While this is fine if we're talking about a store of value such as gold, this is would be really bad for USD.

@foralldogekind @elonmusk @BillyM2k @dogecoin Let's take USD for example. If the Fed just decided to stop printing money altogether, the value of your money will begin to increase in value because of deflation. That's a good thing, right? Nope!

@foralldogekind @elonmusk @BillyM2k @dogecoin One of these positions is putting a cap on Doge. The problem w/ this position is that inflation plays a key part to how well a currency can circulate between people and businesses

@foralldogekind @elonmusk @BillyM2k @dogecoin The big issue really is not that people don't understand crypto, it's that people often don't think of the economic aspects behind it (i.e. inflation rates, consumer adoption, circulation, etc). Because of this people tend to adopt positions that will hurt Doge in the long run

Despite our differences I have huge respect for @BillyM2k trying to cultivate a community of kindness within the dogecoin community. Not many people with platforms as large as theirs seem to spread the same message. Respect and be kind to others, it's that simple.
